Free and Reduced Museum Admission
The Asian Art Museum offers free or reduced admission to its collection galleries and special exhibitions through the programs outlined below. Questions? Contact [email protected].
Membership Program
Asian Art Museum members and their guests enjoy unlimited free admission to the museum’s collection galleries and special exhibitions. Learn more about our world-class membership benefits on the Membership Page.
Current members may reserve free tickets using their membership ID. If you have any questions or need assistance in planning your visit, contact [email protected].
Corporate Partners
Employees of Asian Art Museum’s corporate sponsors and corporate members receive one or more complimentary admission tickets to both the collection galleries and special exhibitions. Check our Institutional Partnerships page to see if your employer is a corporate member. Many of our corporate partners can reserve tickets in advance by visiting our ticketing page and applying the organization’s promotion code upon checkout. If you have questions about corporate benefits or coupon codes, contact [email protected].
Reciprocal Benefits
The Asian Art Museum participates in both the Reciprocal Organization of Associated Museums (ROAM) and North American Reciprocal Museum (NARM) programs. Visitors with ROAM or NARM memberships receive complimentary admission to the collection galleries and only pay the surcharge for special exhibition access. Please bring proof of membership to the museum on the day of your visit. This benefit is limited to same day, walk-up availability. To inquire about special exhibition availability, please speak with a member of the guest experience team at the admissions desk.
Free First Sunday
On the first Sunday of each month, general admission is free and tickets to our special exhibitions are offered at a discounted price of $15. On Free First Sundays, we have limited same-day, walk-up availability for both general admission and special exhibition tickets, so we highly recommend you reserve your tickets in advance.
Caregivers
The Asian Art Museum offers one complimentary guest pass for a caregiver or friend accompanying a visitor with special needs. Complimentary Guest Passes for Caregivers must be requested in-person on the day of your visit. Speak to the Lobby Attendant to request your Caregiver pass.
Museums for All
The Asian Art Museum participates in San Francisco’s Museums for All program. This program grants complimentary general admission to up to four family members. You can upgrade to a special exhibition ticket by paying the surcharge. Please bring either your EBT or MediCal card, and proof of San Francisco residency, to the admissions desk on the day of your visit. This promotion is limited to same-day, walk-up availability.
Active Military
The Asian Art Museum participates in the Blue Star Museums program. Guests with an active Military ID receive complimentary admission to both our collection galleries and special exhibitions. This discount applies to active-duty military personnel and up to five family members. This promotion is limited to same-day, walk-up availability.
Discover and Go
The Discover and Go program provides complimentary passes to California public library cardholders. Guests must reserve their date and time on your local library’s Discover and Go website prior to visiting the museum. These passes grant admission to our collection galleries. Free entry to special exhibitions depends on availability.

2027 Theme
Souls in Motion / Almas en Movimiento
Forty-nine years, and the streets still remember. They remember the drums that echoed through San Francisco before Carnaval SF had a name, calling people together through rhythm and movement. We acknowledge the Ohlone people, the original stewards of this land, whose connection to Place came before us. Then came generations of elders, artists, organizers, dancers, musicians, and dreamers who built something that continues to live. From across the United States, the Caribbean, Latin America, Indigenous communities, and around the world, people brought their cultures, traditions, stories, and dreams to the Bay Area. Together, they shaped the soul of Carnaval SF and wove it into the cultural fabric of this place.

Come celebrate with us at our FREE 2–day family festival & Grand Parade in San Francisco’s Mission District where we will showcase the very best Latin American and Caribbean cultural arts and traditions.
Carnaval San Francisco is the largest multi–cultural celebration on the West Coast.

Festival FAQs
Where is Carnaval San Francisco?
Our free, two–day Festival covers 17 blocks in the Mission District in San Francisco on Harrison Street between 17th Street & 24th Street.
What are the dates of the festival?
The festival is on May 29 & 30, 2027.
What are the festival hours?
The festival opens at 11 AM and closes at 6 PM.
What kind of vendors will be at the festival?
You will experience 250 exhibitors, 50 food vendors, and 5 pavilions offering international cuisine, artisan goods, and community arts workshops and services.
What activities are at the festival?
Enjoy entertainment at our four DJ Block Parties, five stages, Kids Zone, Drum Pavilion, and Skate Jam skateboarding area.
We will also offer a lowrider car show, MWH/Webcor Job Fair, and the Kaiser Health & Wellness Pavilion, and much more.
Is there food at the festival?
Yes. 50 vendors will line the streets with international cuisine from Mexico, Central & South America, the Caribbean, and much more.
Is alcohol allowed at the festival?
No, however, there are designated alcohol gardens throughout the festival serving beer, wine, tequila, and other drinks.
Where can I see your live performances?
Enjoy international music on our five stages and four DJ block parties. Full festival lineup here!
How do I find my favorite food truck or craft artisan?
You can find your favorite vendors on our festival map.
Where is the info booth?
Our Info Booth is on Harrison at 19th Street.
Where is the first aid station?
The First Aid station is on 19th Street between Harrison and Treat Street.
Are pets Allowed?
Pets are not permitted at Carnaval San Francisco. Only trained service animals assisting individuals with disabilities are allowed on event grounds. All service animals must be harnessed, leashed, or tethered unless these devices interfere with the animal’s work or the individual’s disability. Handlers are responsible for maintaining control of their service animal at all times and for cleaning up after them. Leashes should not extend beyond six feet in length.
Please note that the Parade and Festival environments are often loud, crowded, and hot. Handlers should use discretion in determining whether the setting is appropriate for their service animal’s safety and well-being.
Is there a festival map?
Festival map coming soon!
Parade FAQs
Where is the Grand Parade?
The Grand Parade covers 20 blocks in San Francisco’s historic Latino Cultural District in the Mission, beginning at the corner of 24th and Bryant streets, proceeding west to Mission Street, heading north on Mission to 15th Street, turning east on 15th and concluding at South Van Ness Avenue.
When is the Grand Parade?
The Grand Parade is on Sunday, May 24, 2026 and runs from 10:00 AM – 2:00 PM.
Is Grand Parade seating available?
Yes! Ticket link coming soon.
Where is the Grandstand Seating?
The Grand Stand general seating area will be located outside, in front of the Gray Area Theatre (2665 Mission St, SF) as well as on the corner of 22nd and Mission (2601 Mission St, SF). With your ticket you can enter from either side.
The Grand Stand premier seating area will be located in front of The Hall SF Bar & Billiards (2565 Mission St, SF), next to the Parade Judges Stage. Enjoy the electrifying performances next to the judges!
Is Grandstand seating wheelchair accessibility available?
Yes. Wheelchair accessibility is available at the grandstand seating area.
Is reserved seating available?
Tickets are for general admission–no reserve seating available.
Who is in the Grand Parade?
See our parade lineup!
Where will the Grand Parade be broadcast?
The Grand Parade will be broadcast live on KPIX/CBS 5. Stay tuned for a link to the live broadcast on Sunday, May 24, 2026 at 10 AM.
Are pets allowed?
Pets are not permitted at Carnaval San Francisco. Only trained service animals assisting individuals with disabilities are allowed on event grounds. All service animals must be harnessed, leashed, or tethered unless these devices interfere with the animal’s work or the individual’s disability. Handlers are responsible for maintaining control of their service animal at all times and for cleaning up after them. Leashes should not extend beyond six feet in length.
Please note that the Parade and Festival environments are often loud, crowded, and hot. Handlers should use discretion in determining whether the setting is appropriate for their service animal’s safety and well-being.
Is there a Parade Map?
Parade map coming soon!
Travel & Lodging
Can I get there via BART?
Getting to Carnaval in San Francisco’s vibrant Mission District is easy with BART!
Entrances are at 16th & Harrison and 24th & Harrison.
To get to the Carnaval festivities in the Mission, you can take the BART (Bay Area Rapid Transit) and get off at either the 16th Street or 24th Street station. From there, it’s just a short walk East to the heart of the event.
Driving and parking are highly discouraged during the event due to street closures and high attendance.
Can I get there via MUNI?
Getting to Carnaval in San Francisco’s vibrant Mission District is easy with Muni!
Entrances are at 16th & Harrison and 24th & Harrison.
You can take various Muni lines into the Mission District and walk to the entrances at 16th & Harrison and 24th & Harrison.
Reroutes: 12, 14, 12R, 22, 27, 33, 48, 49, 55, 67
Take a look at Muni’s reroute page.
Driving and parking are highly discouraged during the event due to street closures and high attendance.
Is there lodging nearby?
Yes. Carnaval San Francisco’s official hotel is BEI Hotel, located at 50 8th St, San Francisco, CA 94103.
They will take your inquiries 24/7 at 415-626-6103.

Parade Judges
Judge Roberto Borrell
Roberto Borrell has over fifty years of experience performing and teaching Afro-Cuban Folkloric Dance and Cuban Popular Dance in Havana, Cuba and in the United States. Born in Havana, he became a master of Danzón, Son, Son-Montuno, Guaracha, and the Cha-Cha-Cha at a young age. His stylish dancing earned him an invitation to join Cuba’s Conjunto Folklórico Nacional where he was schooled in the traditional Orisha songs, dances, and rhythms by the most renowned Afro-Cuban folkloric dancers and percussionists of the time.
Roberto has directed musical groups for over 30 years, from his early days with his own group in Cuba, Union Cienfueguera, to his popular San Francisco-based Danzón orchestra, Orquesta la Moderna Tradición.
Judge Stacie Powers Cuéllar
Anastacia Powers Cuéllar has been a part of the Mission District Arts Community since 1983. Her credits include Production and Tour Manager for the San Francisco Mime Troupe, Business Manager for Dr. Loco’s Rockin’ Jalapeño Band and Managing Director of Dance Mission Theater. In February 2012 she became Executive Director of Brava! for Women in the Arts and Brava Theater Center until she retired in June of 2025.
During her tenure at Brava she oversaw not only the revitalization of the Theater Center and its programming, but also grew their Fiscal Sponsorship program to support the revitalization of Carnaval SF, the founding of the Latino Cultural District and the community partnership between the Latino Task Force and SF General Hospital’s COVID response program
Judge John Calloway
Dr. John Calloway is a nationally recognized multi-instrumentalist/composer who for 40 years led a dual career in education. He has performed in the Bay Area with John Santos, Mark Levine, and Marcus Shelby along with internationally known artists such as Cachao.
He was the co-founder and music director of the Latin Jazz Youth Ensemble of San Francisco from 2001-2024 while serving as an educator, SFUSD arts administrator, and San Francisco Arts Commissioner. He also founded the Afro-Cuban Ensemble of San Francisco State University in 1999, stepping down as its only director after 25 years. He taught in SF public schools for over 30 years.
Judge Jazz-Ylaine Baptiste
Queen Jazz-Ylaine Baptiste is a Cultural Architect, facilitator of ancestral remembrance, and Founder & Director of Samba Journeys Cultural Arts Institute in Oakland, California. A second-generation dancer with over 20 years of experience in Samba and Afro-Brazilian dance, she is recognized for her commitment to honoring the roots of Samba through education, embodied practice, and cultural exchange.
She competed in Samba and Carnaval competitions at the local, regional, national, and international levels between 2010 and 2025, winning many titles and bringing her deep cultural knowledge, lived experience, and integrity to the art form.
Judge Jessica Maria Recinos
Jessica Maria Recinos has been part of the San Francisco Carnaval scene since she was a teenager – first as a performer, then growing into a community leader and culture bearer. Her dance journey began in the streets and studios of the Mission and Excelsior, training across styles and building lasting connections that now span nationally and globally.
As the founder of Rising Rhythm, Jessica blends movement, music, and fashion to celebrate the creative power of Black and Brown communities. Her professional arts experience gives her a sharp, detail-oriented eye, keeping things competitive, fresh, and exciting. She’s passionate about bringing new ideas to Carnaval while honoring its roots, always pushing to elevate the experience for everyone involved

Castro Street Fair 2026: A View from Above
Posted on 10/12/202610/14/2026
On the streets, it felt incredible. From the sky? Absolutely epic! Take in the energy of the 52nd Castro Street Fair from a whole new perspective.
View this post on Instagram
A post shared by Castro Street Fair (@castrostreetfair)
And with that, CSF 2026 is a wrap! Thanks to our artists and musicians who filled our streets with joyful music and color-filled connection; to our nonprofit beneficiaries for all their essential and inspiring work for San Francisco and the Bay Area; to our vendors and exhibitors for proving the power and vitality of the small business community; to our sponsors and partners for helping make this Fair one of the biggest in years... and to everyone who showed up, boogied down and shouted to the world that this is Where We Belong.
Until we meet again: Sunday, October 3, 2027 🏳️‍🌈
(Huge thanks to JJ Meeks (IG) for sharing this stunning drone footage from the 2026 Fair!)
Welcome to the 52nd Annual Castro Street Fair
Posted on 10/04/202610/14/2026
We’re so happy to have you with us for another day of community, celebration, and joy in the heart of the Castro!
This year’s theme, “Where We Belong,” reflects what the Castro has meant to generations of LGBTQIA+ people: a place to find community, feel seen, live openly, and connect with one another. It’s also a reminder that belonging is something we create together — where trans people belong, where drag belongs, where allies belong, where chosen family belongs, and where hope belongs.
Since Harvey Milk founded the Fair in 1974, the Castro Street Fair has brought together neighbors, artists, performers, local businesses, community organizations, friends, and allies. More than five decades later, that spirit is still at the heart of everything we do.
The Fair is also a celebration of the merchants and small businesses that give the Castro its energy and character. We hope you’ll explore the neighborhood, shop local, and support the businesses that help keep the Castro vibrant year-round.
Just as importantly, the Fair gives back. Since 1998, we’ve distributed more than $1.6 million to local nonprofit beneficiaries, supporting organizations that strengthen and serve our community. When you arrive at the Fair, we encourage you to make a donation at the entry gates — your contribution helps us continue that tradition of giving back.
Continue reading “Welcome to the 52nd Annual Castro Street Fair” →
Official Fair After Party at the Castro Theatre
Posted on 10/04/202610/01/2026
The Castro Street Fair may wrap at 6 PM, but the night is just getting started.
Head to the Castro Theatre for the Official Castro Street Fair After Party, presented by Polyglamorous and featuring Octo Octa, BEYA and Mark O’Brien!
It’s the perfect way to keep celebrating this year’s theme, “Where We Belong,” with more music, more dancing and one very iconic Castro backdrop.
Sunday, October 4
Doors: 5:30 PM
Show: 6:00 PM
All ages
$35.25–$65.25 via Ticketmaster
Come for the Fair. Stay for the dance floor!
Entertainment: Five Ways to Find Your Groove in 2026
Posted on 09/30/202610/02/2026
From big-stage performances to country-western line dancing, indie alt sounds and family-friendly fun, this year’s Castro Street Fair has something happening around nearly every corner.
Check the full lineups here, and get ready to dance!
Catch the energy at the Castro Stage, discover the eclectic mix at Queer AF, dance your way through the Collingwood Stage, and welcome our very first Family Zone with face painting, juggling, balloon twisting and Drag Queen Story Time.
And of course, longtime Fair favorite Sundance Saloon brings two-steppin’, line dancin’ and boot-scootin’ to a packed dance floor at the Castro Theatre parking lot!
Donate. Get the sticker. Save a buck.
Posted on 09/29/202610/02/2026
Here’s one more reason to donate at the Castro Street Fair gates: your 2026 donation sticker gets you $1 off drinks at our Official Bar Partners throughout Fair Day.
Just flash your sticker at Beaux, Copper Kitchen & Microbrewery, Midnight Sun, or QBar and enjoy that little discount while you’re out exploring the Fair.
All four partners are located inside the Fair footprint and Castro Entertainment Zone...and yes, you can take that drink for a stroll. The Castro is an official Entertainment Zone, so guests 21+ can enjoy eligible to-go drinks — no glass or metal containers — from participating bar partners throughout the activated Fair footprint.
Best of all, your donation helps support the Fair’s nonprofit beneficiaries — cocktails and philanthropy, a winning pair. Cheers!
New Voices, Returning Favorites, One Big Fair
Posted on 09/29/202610/02/2026
This year’s Castro Street Fair is bringing new energy, returning favorites, and plenty of reasons to dance in the street.
We’re thrilled to welcome San Francisco Black Pride to the Castro Stage at Castro and Market Streets for a special block of programming celebrating Black LGBTQ+ artists and community. SF Black Pride grew from an idea sparked by local artist and organizer LBXX (Gyasi Curry) and launched its first Pride Week in 2025.
At the Fair, the SF Black Pride lineup currently includes Ms. Love O, The Junior and LBXX, with programming still evolving and subject to change.
You’ll also find entertainment at the Collingwood Stage at 18th Street, the Queer AF Stage programmed by Devlin Shand, plus more new and returning artists throughout the Fair.
It all comes together under this year’s theme, “Where We Belong” — because sometimes belonging looks a lot like dancing in the middle of Castro Street with a few thousand of your closest friends.
Golden State Comes to the Castro
Posted on 09/25/202610/03/2026
The Castro Street Fair is thrilled to welcome the Golden State Warriors and Golden State Valkyries as new sponsors of this year’s Fair! And we’re sending an extra-big congratulations to the Valkyries as they head into the playoffs — what a season, and what a way to make some Bay Area history.
On Sunday, October 4, both teams will be right in the heart of the action with booths located directly in front of the iconic Castro Theatre, next to the Castro Street Fair Info + Merch Booth, directly in front of the iconic Castro Theatre. Stop by, say hello, grab your Fair merch, and soak up some serious Golden State energy.
It’s a pretty perfect matchup: Bay Area sports, Castro community, and a whole lot of pride. We’re excited to welcome the Warriors and Valkyries to the Fair — and even more excited to celebrate together in the place Where We Belong.
52nd CASTRO STREET FAIR REVEALS FULL 2026 KEY ART
Posted on 09/10/202610/03/2026
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
Original artwork by Ece Kalabak, with graphic design and campaign adaptations by Özgür Baltutan, will shape the Fair’s visual identity with this year’s theme, “Where We Belong”
SAN FRANCISCO — September 9, 2026 — The Castro Street Fair is proud to share the full key art for its 52nd annual celebration, bringing this year’s theme, “Where We Belong,” to life through an original illustration by artist Ece Kalabak.
The newly revealed artwork will serve as the foundation of the Fair’s 2026 visual identity and marketing campaign, appearing across advertising, social media, digital communications, print materials, merchandise, signage and other creative elements leading up to the Fair taking place on Sunday, October 4, 2026, from 11 a.m. to 6 p.m. in San Francisco’s Castro neighborhood.

52nd ANNUAL CASTRO STREET FAIR ANNOUNCES 2026 THEME: “WHERE WE BELONG”
Posted on 06/01/2026
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
Founded by Harvey Milk, San Francisco’s legacy street fair returns Sunday, October 4, celebrating the Castro as a place of joy, freedom, community and belonging
SAN FRANCISCO, CA — June 1, 2026 — On this first day of Pride Month, the Castro Street Fair announces “Where We Belong” as the theme for its 52nd annual celebration, taking place Sunday, October 4, 2026, from 11:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. in the heart of San Francisco’s Castro District.
Founded by Harvey Milk in 1974, the Castro Street Fair began as a celebration of gay-owned businesses and the vitality of the Castro neighborhood. More than five decades later, the Fair continues that legacy by bringing together LGBTQIA+ people, neighbors, families, artists, performers, merchants, community organizations and allies for a joyful celebration of queer life and community connection.
This year’s theme, “Where We Belong,” honors the Castro as a place where generations of LGBTQIA+ people have found community, safety, visibility and joy, and affirms that the neighborhood remains a beacon of freedom and diversity today.
The theme also creates space for a broader declaration of belonging: Where trans people belong. Where drag belongs. Where chosen family belongs. Where hope belongs. Where we belong.
Continue reading “52nd ANNUAL CASTRO STREET FAIR ANNOUNCES 2026 THEME: “WHERE WE BELONG”” →
Celebrate Harvey Milk Day with a Donation!
Posted on 05/22/2026
Happy Birthday, Harvey!
Today would have been Harvey Milk’s 96th birthday.
In his short time here, Harvey created a legacy that is still felt today. For 52 years, we have continued his tradition of bringing the community together through the Castro Street Fair — a celebration rooted in joy, visibility, and neighborhood pride.
Harvey believed in the power of community, and the Castro Street Fair remains a living tribute to that vision. As he says in the video “A street fair should be — for the neighborhood, about the neighborhood, and by the neighborhood.”
Please help us continue supporting Harvey’s vision for the Castro Street Fair with a donation. All donations will support this year’s fair on Sunday, October 4, 2026.

Choy Sun Doe
The 2027 Choy Sun Doe Day is scheduled for Saturday, Feb. 6.
About
Under the auspices of the SF Chinese Chamber of Commerce, Choy Suns will grace Chinatown and pass out thousands of “Lai Sees” to eagerly waiting children. All the “Lai Sees” will contain a chocolate gold coin. Additionally, some will have either money or a gift certificate that can be redeemed for a toy.
Choy Sun, the god of wealth, is a deity that every Chinese person welcomes. He blesses everyone he encounters with much prosperity and abundant wealth.
Traditionally, “Lai Sees” (red envelopes) are passed out to children and unmarried
persons during Chinese New Year as a good luck symbol, with the belief that the more “Lai Sees” one passes out, the more good luck will be returned.

FAQ
When is the Chinese New Year Parade?
The San Francisco Chinese New Year Parade, celebrating the Year of the Ram, will be on Saturday, February 20, 2027 and starts at 5:15 PM from 2nd and Market St. It is a free event for all to attend but tickets must be purchased to sit in the bleacher sections.
What is the Parade Route?
The parade starts off at 2nd and Market Streets, goes around Union Square and ends at Kearny Street & Columbus Ave. The distance of the parade route is approximately 1.3 miles. The parade is a free event for all to attend and you may stand anywhere on the parade route, behind the barricades, to watch the parade. The following map also shows the location of crossing points through the parade route. These areas can be used to safely cross the parade route but must be kept clear for emergency personnel. Please do not stand in these areas to watch the parade. In order to maintain the flow of the parade, Local law enforcement and parade personnel will instruct guests when it will be safe to cross over. Please follow their instructions. If you have purchased a bleacher ticket, and we highly recommend you do, the following map also shows the locations of your bleacher areas.
How can one participate in the Chinese New Year Parade?
If your organization is interested in participating in the parade, please contact the parade office using the contact form at: https://chineseparade.com/#contact
Where is the best place to view the parade and what time should we arrive?
The entire parade route is an excellent place to view the parade but it does get more crowded as you get closer to Chinatown. If you purchased bleacher tickets, we strongly encourage you to check-in to your assigned section by 4:00 PM. Please note that SFPD will begin closing streets around 3pm and we are not responsible for any delays this may cause you to arrive to your assigned bleacher section on time.
How do I purchase bleacher seats?
We have partnered with Eventeny to provide digital tickets to our attendees. You may purchase tickets from our tickets page. Be careful of scammers, we only sell tickets online through Eventeny which you may access through our tickets page. All ticket sales are final and are non-refundable.
Accessible seating within each bleacher section is available for purchase at the same price as standard bleacher seating. If you require wheelchair seating accommodations, please select an ‘ADA Section’ ticket for your preferred bleacher section when purchasing.
I purchased tickets online through Eventeny, where can find my tickets?
Tickets will be e-mailed to you or available within your Eventeny App for your mobile device.
Where are the Bleachers located?
Section A is located at Kearny Street (between Washington & Jackson Streets)
Section B is located at Kearny Street (between California & Sacramento Streets)
Section C is located at Post St. (between Grant Ave and Kearny Streets)
Section E is located at Geary St (between Stockton and Powell Streets)
Every bleacher ticket will have an assigned location and you may sit anywhere you like within your assigned location. Due to the early street closures by law enforcement and the crowds which build up, please try to be near your Bleacher Section area by 4:00 pm.
Important: Your receipt will not permit you to sit in the bleachers, you must present your ticket (QR-Code) at a Check-In station and you will be given a badge to display while you sit within the bleacher areas.
Where are the Wheelchair and Accessible Seating locations?
Designated Accessible Seating is available at street-level along the parade route and within our ticketed bleacher sections. These areas will be clearly marked with banners.
If you purchased an accessible bleacher ticket, you will be seated within your designated bleacher section. If you do not have a ticket, you are welcome to use the free, reserved accessible viewing areas located along the street barricades.
Do I need to purchase a bleacher ticket for my child?
Children 2 and under are free but must sit on the lap of a caregiver with a valid bleacher ticket.
What items are prohibited at the parade?
This is a public event, and we ask that you comply with all local laws and regulations regarding prohibited items, such as weapons, firearms, explosives, and drones. Additionally, out of consideration for others, we request that large items that may encroach on others’ space—such as oversized cushions, coolers, pets, selfie sticks, or camera tripods—are not brought into the bleacher sections.
Is the parade going to be cancelled if it rains? How long is the parade?
No, the parade will not be cancelled if it rains and the parade is approximately 2-1/2 hours. Please dress accordingly to the weather.
What is the best way to get to the parade?
We strongly suggest everyone take public transportation. For more details on transportation options, click here.
Where are the portable restrooms?
Portables will be placed throughout the parade route typically close to the bleacher areas.
What if I have more questions?
For further questions, please contact the Parade Office @ (415) 889-8891 or info@chineseparade.com

Step Inside the 2026 Showcase
The 2026 San Francisco Decorator Showcase welcomed visitors inside an extraordinary Queen Anne-style Victorian residence at 2315 Broadway Street in Pacific Heights. Built in 1897 and designed by architect Moses J. Lyon, the historic home spanned nearly 10,000 square feet and served as the setting for the iconic design event. Reimagined by the Bay Area’s top interior and landscape designers, the Showcase House celebrated creativity, craftsmanship, and community.

https://downtownsf.org/things-to-do/drag.text:
4 Shows. 13 Performers. 100% San Francisco.
Buckle up, buttercup! Drag Me Downtown, San Francisco's signature pop-up drag show series, returns every Friday for Pride 2026!
Produced by the Downtown SF Partnership in collaboration with Bobby Friday—the creative force behind Haus of Friday—we’re celebrating year four with our most iconic destinations yet. Expect fierce lip-syncs by your favorite Bay Area performers, flirty cocktails, and a whole lotta glam.
Drag Me Downtown is FREE WITH RSVP. Pre-registration also secures your exclusive Drag Swag at the door to spice up your lewk (while supplies last).
As always, we party with purpose. For the third year running, we’re proud to partner with The Transgender District—the first legally recognized district of its kind in the world, right here in SF. Upon registration, we invite you to contribute a $10 donation to support their essential community programs.
FREE WITH RSVP
Featured Performers
Bobby Friday
The creative force behind Haus of Friday, specializing in event production, hosting, & custom wigs. Known for their Fierce, Fabulous, & Fresh to Death! aesthetic, Bobby uses their platform to serve the community & holds the title of SF Grand Duchess 48, & was crowned Miss California Gold & Miss Castro Club in 2020. You can find her at venues across SF & as a host at 620 Jones Drag Brunch.
Learn More
Curveball
A little bit ditsy and a whole lotta diva, she’s got the curves and she brings it every ball! Curveball is known for her big hair, big smile, and big naturals. San Francisco has shaped Curvy into a queen who is beautifully stupid and stupidly beautiful. She's here to remind you that everyday we get the gift of showing up as whoever we want to be in this world – so you show up as fabulous as you can! You can find her at Lookout as the cohost of Lips & Lashes Drag Brunch, and strutting her legs in venues across the Bay Area.
Learn More
Hennessy Williams
Hennessy Williams is an Oakland-based Chinese American drag performer who performs as both a king and queen. Their art is rooted in storytelling, dance, genderfuckery, & queer joy. A self-taught seamstress & dancer, they often create their own costumes & choreography. They are the reigning Mx. NorCal Quing Pageant winner & the creator/host of ROYALES, an all-BIPOC Drag King show. They headlined the 2023 Austin International Drag Festival & have graced stages like Oaklash Drag festival and ThrustFest.
Learn More
Hera Wynn
Hera Wynn (she/her) is a trans entertainer based in San Francisco and greater Bay Area. For nearly 5 years, she has performed across the West Coast, produced her own events, and opened for pop celebrities. Hera has made her mark on the scene and continues to show exactly why she is the "It Girl" of SF. From her fierce makeup and enchanting performances to her high-energy dancing, she will no doubt leave you wanting more.
Learn More
Jax
Known for their stunts & acrobatics that graced RuPaul’s Drag Race Season 15, Jax is a multidisciplinary artist recently relocated from NYC to the Bay Area. Combining a background in cheerleading & gymnastics with an education in visual arts, Jax performs at a high caliber locally & internationally. A decorated TV lip-sync assassin, Jax holds multiple NYC titles & GLAM Award nominations. Exploring their love of drag alongside video gamesl JAX adapts their persona as an active streamer through twitch and cosplay conventions.
Learn More
King SlayHer
King SlayHer is the premier Drag King of the South Bay & reigning California Male Impersonator Pageant King. He is the creator & host of Sapphic Sundaze, a San Jose-based R&B Sapphic Drag Brunch. After surviving a life-altering accident, King SlayHer embodies strength, resilience, & the unbreakable spirit of disabled Drag Kings everywhere. He inspires others to reclaim their power & take the stage unapologetically.
Learn More
Lisa Frankenstein
The "Eyes of the Bay" & the "High Fem" they/them, Lisa Frankenstein is a self-described weirdo with a decade of decadence under their belt. A critically acclaimed & award-winning performer, they are currently celebrating 10 years of pushing boundaries in the drag scene. Whether serving avant-garde looks or high-concept performance art, Lisa continues to be a captivating fixture of Bay Area nightlife.
Learn More
Madd Dogg 20/20
Madd-Dogg 20/20 has been a driving force in the Bay Area drag king scene since 2006. Crowned Grand Duke of SF in 2017, he is known for his magnetic presence, smooth swagger, & commitment to elevating kings. A natural entertainer & producer, Madd-Dogg co-produces Santa Cruz favorites like The Shug Shack & MAHvelous Drag Brunch. Alongside partner Miss Shugana, he also helped revive the iconic Women’s Weekend Russian River. Whether mentoring or performing, Madd-Dogg always brings heart & style.
Learn More
Mercedez Munro
Absolute Empress 52 of San Francisco & matriarch of La Maison de Munro, Mercedez Munro is a dedicated entertainer, activist, & philanthropist. She prides herself on preserving "old school" drag while embracing the new. With 43 career pageant wins, she also promotes "Us!" at Beaux alongside Terrill Grimes Munro. Held every second-to-last Saturday, the event highlights QTLGBTQIA+ BIPOC excellence throughout the Bay. Mercedez is a true icon of community service & stagecraft.
Learn More
Miss Shugana
Dazzling audiences since 2013, Miss Shugana offers a signature mix of charm, camp, & joyful mischief. A beloved queen of the faux variety, she is deeply committed to community & philanthropy. As a former Duchess of SF, she helped raise over $100,000 for charitable causes. Today, she produces Santa Cruz favorites like The Shug Shack & MAHvelous Drag Brunch. Alongside partner Madd-Dogg 20/20, she helped resurrect Women’s Weekend Russian River for the sapphic community.
Learn More
Nicki Jizz
Nicki Jizz is the winner of the Drag Queen of the Year pageant & a 5x "Best Drag Queen of the Bay Area" recipient. She is the host of "Reparations," the iconic, 5x award-winning all-Black drag show at Oasis. Whether entertaining massive crowds at nightclubs, brunches, or roller rinks, Nicki brings unmatched humor & glamour. A queen of the people, she strives to uplift QTBIPOC performers on the many stages she produces. Nicki is more than just a Queen—she is THAT GIRL.
Learn More
Saiyohni Gray
Saiyohni Gray is a Bay Area queen & dancing diva who lives to twirl & serve sickening looks. With bold energy & a flair for the dramatic, she brings unforgettable movement & attitude to every stage she touches. A true force of nature in the local scene, Saiyohni captivates audiences with her high-caliber performances & magnetic personality. Prepare to be enchanted by a queen who knows exactly how to command a room.
Learn More
Todd Hotty
Todd Hotty is half human & half hotty, spicing the tea since 2006 and now igniting stages across SF & the West Coast. Rooted in community service, he uses his drag as a platform for philanthropy, uplifting & protecting the community he loves. Todd believes embracing every version of yourself is the key to loving others. Catch this seasoned entertainer bringing heart and heat to every performance!
Learn More

Plus, an elevated menu of bites including salmon tartare, tots with crème fraîche and caviar (vegan available), and more!

FAQs
Is Drag Me Downtown an all ages event?
We love seeing "little icons" in the crowd! Everyone is welcome, but keep in mind that our shows are adult in spirit, featuring plenty of sass and flirty banter. We leave parental discretion to you. If you are planning to sip on an alcoholic beverage (or two), please be prepared to flash your ID upon arrival.
Is Drag Me Downtown held outdoors?
June 5th at 101 California Plaza will be outdoors, June 12th at the Ferry Building back plaza will be outdoors, June 19th at The Conservatory at One Sansome will be indoors, and June 26th at The Merchants Exchange will be indoors.
Will there be food and beverages available?
Yes! Each venue will be offering a beverages and bites available for purchase.
Will there be an ATM on site?
While there are not ATMs directly on site at our participating venues, there are numerous in the surrounding Downtown area. Please plan in advance and come prepared to TIP YOUR PERFORMERS!

With bold energy & a flair for the dramatic, she brings unforgettable movement & attitude to every stage she touches. A true force of nature in the local scene, Saiyohni captivates audiences with her high-caliber performances & magnetic personality. Prepare to be enchanted by a queen who knows exactly how to command a room. Learn More

Todd Hotty Todd Hotty is half human & half hotty, spicing the tea since 2006 and now igniting stages across SF & the West Coast. Rooted in community service, he uses his drag as a platform for philanthropy, uplifting & protecting the community he loves. Todd believes embracing every version of yourself is the key to loving others. Catch this seasoned entertainer bringing heart and heat to every performance! Learn More

Press Release: EArth Day San Francisco Continues At The New Farm
Source: EIN News
Annual Festival will showcase unique community resources at Hunter’s Point landmark
Organizers of San Francisco’s popular Earth Day festival (EDSF) have a history of honoring and partnering with other major events and initiatives such as Save The Redwoods League and March for Science, and for the second time will hold their annual event in Bayview/Hunter’s Point at The New Farm (https://thenewfarmsf.org) on Sunday, April 19, from Noon to 6 PM.
“Earth Day is really every day at the New Farm,” says Andy Pollack, the director of San Francisco’s emerging community garden and mixed-use public space by the San Francisco Bay. “The style of the festival, which offers both contemporary music, cultural programming and environmental education, represents our exact mission and brings greater attention to the work we’re doing here all the time. Our core mission is to create a model where the community and the natural world can come together.”
The New Farm was established in 2020 by the Green City Project with community partners Bay Natives Nursery and Heron’s Head Nursery to covert an abandoned asphalt lot to a beautiful natural environment showcasing cutting edge organic farming. The farm features many plants and vegetables with a special emphasis on California native plants; chickens and other farm animals run free during a normal day. The New Farm’s neighbors include Heron’s Head Park with its environmental center, and City Grazing which offers grazing goats for rent. The inspiration and model for farm organizers is the Crossroads Community Farm which thrived in San Francisco from 1974 to 1987. Founders Bonnie Sherk (a noted San Francisco artist) and Jack Wickert created a community center which brought the country to the city; Fort Mason recent presented a major exhibit of Sherk’s work.
“We’re continuing to highlight the Green City Project and The New Farm because we want the entire Bay Area to experience it personally,” says EDSF steering committee chair Monalisa Wallace. “Free and open to the public, visitors can learn about native plants, see chickens and goats up close and discover urban farming tips and other homesteading skills.”
The entertainment and music stage has always been a big part of the festival and kicks off with a dance performance by the Temple of Isis, a local goddess community. Local favorites Jordan Feinstein, Pamela Parker, Rojai and the Third Thursday Band, have curated a day long dance party representing the unique funky, jazzy, rock and electronic fusion sound that has long been a part of the San Francisco music scene. New Farm is becoming one of the hottest new music venues in the city (https://www.sfgate.com/sf-culture/article/The-coolest-new-music-venue-in-SF-is-a-farm-in-16406357.php).
“The best and most meaningful music is collaboration of artists and community,” says Cisco Disco, a 19-year-old emerging artist. “We are coming together on Earth Day for the love of our planet and each other.”
Speakers include renown San Francisco activist and civil rights attorney Angela Alioto (also the daughter of San Francisco’s 36th mayor, Joseph Alioto) on the history of Earth Day in San Francisco, and Judy Berg Goldhalf, co-founder with husband Peter Berg of Planet Drum, on biodiversity and bioregional awareness.
The land is leased to the nonprofit New Farm organization by the Port of San Francisco for the sole purpose of producing and hosting community activities for environmental education and cultural programs. Community organizations can reserve the space free of charge for events and educational activities. All of The New Farm’s revenue comes from donations, and there is a GoFundMe page for the earth day event: https://www.gofundme.com/f/support-the-new-farm-at-earthdaysf-2026 .
The festival is free and will also feature a wide variety of family-friendly activities, food, an art gallery and resources.
The history Of Earth Day SF
Inspired by the first Earth Day in 1970, Earth Day San Francisco has year after year been an anchor leader in a movement now spanning over 190 countries and over 22,000 events around the world. The SF Earth Day core team has been producing Earth Day SF every year since 2011, with music festivals, teach-ins and environmental activism. The Endangered Species Act, the National Environment Policy Act, the Clean Air and Clean Water Acts all have their roots in the first Earth Day. Earth Day SF gathered thousands of signatures for Proposition 37 in 2012 to label genetically modified foods known to be high in chemical residues. Each year we focus on pressing environmental issues and foster grassroots collaboration for the planet.

Held annually between the Golden Gate Bridge and Alcatraz, the San Francisco Fleet Week Air Show Presented by United Airlines brings world-class aviation to one of the most iconic settings in the world.
At the heart of the Air Show is Marina Green, home to the Marina Green Festival Center. General Admission is free. Unbeatable waterfront hospitality is available through the Air Show Network VIP Experience.
Headlined by the U.S. Navy Blue Angels, the Air Show is also the only show in the United States to feature a commercial airliner, the United 777, performing a fully choreographed aerial demonstration over the Bay.

Pop-Ups on the Plaza: Juneteenth on the Waterfront
Sunday, June 7, 2026, 11:00 am - 4:00 pm
Pop-Ups on the Plaza Ferry Plaza
Celebrate local Black-owned businesses at the 6th annual Juneteenth on the Waterfront on Sunday, June 7. Kick off a month of Juneteenth celebrations in San Francisco with a day of delicious food, crafts, and community in the front plaza of the Ferry Building. Savor handcrafted foods and drinks from Black entrepreneurs, shop for local crafts at the In The Black pop-up market, and enjoy fun activities for the whole family. Entry is free and open to the public, with food and drink available for purchase.
Pop-Ups on the Plaza is a series of events celebrating Bay Area BIPOC entrepreneurs, including businesses in Foodwise’s Building Equity program. Pop-Ups on the Plaza is a Port sponsored event brought to you by Foodwise. This program is proudly funded in partnership with the San Francisco Human Rights Commission. Additional support is provided by the Ferry Building.

Celebrate Juneteenth in San Francisco
Juneteenth National Independence Day (June 19) is a federal holiday celebrating the anniversary of Black emancipation in the United States. It is honored on the anniversary of June 19, 1865, when freedom from slavery was proclaimed in the state of Texas. Celebrate Juneteenth in San Francisco throughout the month:
June 13: Juneteenth SF Freedom Celebration in the Fillmore
June 20: Juneteenth Parade
June 21: Juneteenth Bayview and Father’s Day Festival
Building Equity Program & Pop-Ups on the Plaza
Pop-Ups on the Plaza is an initiative of Foodwise’s Building Equity program. Foodwise and our community partners, En2action, In The Black, La Cocina, and Mandela Partners, are proudly committed to uplifting and advancing equity for BIPOC, immigrant, and limited-resource entrepreneurs across the Bay Area.

Ferry Plaza Farmers Market
The Ferry Plaza Farmers Market is a triweekly California Certified Farmers Market operated by Foodwise at the San Francisco Ferry Building on Saturday, Tuesday, and Thursday, year round. Since 1993, the market has served as a crucial link between urban dwellers and local farmers, renowned for its diverse offering of delicious, high-quality products from California’s cutting-edge sustainable growers, food makers, and chefs, as well as education programs to connect eaters of all ages with our local foodshed.

Mission Community Market: Thursday
3 pm – 7 pm (mid March – mid November) | Founded in July 2010, Mission Community Market (aka Mission Mercado) is an open-air market made up of farmers, small local businesses, and community programs, promoting family health and creating a fun, beautiful public space for the Mission District. This beloved neighborhood market supports about 25 small local farms and businesses, and provides healthy food access for Mission residents through programs like Market Match, which doubles shoppers’ CalFresh EBT benefits. Since 2018, Foodwise has been honored to support this vibrant neighborhood market with deep roots in the Mission community.

https://goldengateparkband.org/.title: Golden Gate Park Band
https://goldengateparkband.org/.text:
San Francisco’s
Golden Gate Park Band
Since 1882
The Soul of the City
The Golden Gate Park Band
San Francisco’s Original Multi-Cultural Art’s Organization
When the Golden Gate Park Band was formed in 1882, San Francisco was still a very young city composed of many diverse immigrant communities. Throughout the Band’s history we have partnered with many organizations and featured themed concerts that celebrate the various cultures that are part of San Francisco. In this way cultural traditions are shared publicly for the whole community to enjoy. We are part of the proud heritage of San Francisco as a city of inclusivity that celebrates the heritage and cultures of the people that make it their home.
Each season, the Band collaborates with various ethnic, community and arts groups throughout San Francisco to bring in dance troupes, singers, and guest ensembles. GGPB features soloists from within its membership as well as guest artists.
Our season runs from April through September, with shows every Sunday plus July 4 and Labor Day at the Spreckels Temple of Music in the Music Concourse of Golden Gate Park.
View the Schedule
Music Director, Dr. German Gonzalez
Welcome from our Music Director, Dr. German Gonzalez!
Welcome to the 2026 season of the Golden Gate Park Band! We proudly present 25 high-quality concerts designed to appeal to audiences of all ages.
Our weekly performances are often compared to the Boston Pops—but performed outdoors by a vibrant ensemble of wind and percussion instruments. Dressed in our timeless red blazers and hats, we delight audiences with a wide variety of music including classical favorites, marches, jazz, pop, folk songs, film music, and Broadway show tunes.
Throughout the season we feature special in-house and guest soloists, sing-alongs, and other opportunities for audience participation. Every concert offers a unique program, so you can expect a fresh musical experience each time you attend.
Bring a picnic lunch, a blanket, and dress in layers. Sundays in Golden Gate Park are lively, so we recommend using public transit when possible. After the concert, consider visiting the nearby de Young Museum, the California Academy of Sciences, or renting bicycles to explore the park. The gardens of Golden Gate Park are beautiful year-round.
Be sure to sign up for our email newsletter to receive weekly updates throughout the season. Thank you for your continued support of the Golden Gate Park Band.
Where Music
Meets Community
For generations, this band has been part of the rhythm of San Francisco life. Their mission is simple but powerful: keep great music accessible, keep the tradition alive, and keep welcoming new audiences into the circle.
Come out and join the tradition!
View the Schedule
Support a
Living Piece of
San Francisco’s
Musical History
For over a century, the Golden Gate Park Band has filled San Francisco with free, world-class music — a tradition made possible by listeners like you. Sponsored in part by the San Francisco Recreation and Parks Department, the Band still depends on community generosity. Your donation helps sustain professional musicians, expand programming, and keep this treasured cultural tradition free for all. Help us keep the music playing.
Become part of the tradition.

Festival Details
WHEN Fri Oct 2, Sat Oct 3, and Sun Oct 4, 2026
WHERE Hellman Hollow, Lindley & Marx meadows in Golden Gate Park, San Francisco, CA.
IS THERE A LIVE WEBCAST?
Yes, we will be streaming the Banjo, Swan, Towers of Gold, Rooster, Arrow and Horseshoe Hill Stages. Tune into HSBTV.
WHAT TIME ARE WE ALLOWED IN?
Entrances will open at 11am on Friday, and 9am Saturday & Sunday. Performances end at 7pm daily.
Festival Entrances
1) JFK Drive and Transverse Drive
2) Fulton Street and 30th Avenue
3) JFK Drive and 36th Avenue

Entrances will open at 11am on Friday, 9am Saturday and Sunday. Performances end at 7pm daily.
For the safety of all patrons, security measures in place include walking through body scanners and may include a physical search of bags and belongings. SFPD, K9 and Tactical Units will be positioned inside and outside the venue.
HSB encourages the use of public transportation or any alternative to personal vehicles.

Restroom Facilities
There will be port-a-potties on site. See the map for locations.
Free Water
Free water refills will be available:
Near the permanent bathrooms (between the Banjo Stage and Arrow Meadow)
McClaren Pass (between the Horseshoe Hill and Swan Stages)
Next to JFK Flats concessions
On the North Side of Swan Crossover
Medical Attention & Nearest Hospital
An on-site medical team will be available. The nearest hospital is Health Connection St Mary’s Hospital & Medical Center at 450 Stanyan St, San Francisco, CA – (415) 750-5785
Compost & Recycling
HSB composts and recycles all waste generated over the weekend. We encourage you to help us move closer to being a Zero Waste event by disposing your items in the designated receptacles or pack out what you brought in!
Merchandise
We will be selling HSB t-shirts and merchandise from most artists. Merch booths will be located only at Arrow Meadow, and the Foggy Bottom Cafe.
Lost & Found
Lost and found is located at all four Info booths (see map).
ATMS
HSB is cashless, please use credit or debit cards at our merchandise & food concessions. There will be no ATMs onsite.
Transportation Around the Park
This year we expect the park service to run their shuttle service.
Bike Parking
Please do not lock bikes to trees or traffic poles.
There is no bike valet service and bike parking is at your own risk.
HSB is not responsible for missing or stolen property.
Car Parking
If you park on the street, please respect the neighborhood and DO NOT block driveways! Parking in the neighborhoods surrounding Golden Gate Park is EXTREMELY limited. We highly encourage taking public transport, ride-sharing, biking or walking instead of driving. It is very important that we all respect the neighbors around the park – do NOT block driveways, clean up after yourselves, and keep noise levels down. Remember that people live here and do not use yards as toilets or trash cans.
Similar to last year, we expect paid parking, run by local PTAs, to be available on a first come first serve basis at a few lots on Saturday and Sunday. Last year those lots included:
George Washington High School – 600 32nd Ave. [enter at 30th Ave. between Geary & Anza]
Argonne – 680 18th Ave. [enter at Cabrillo between 17th Ave. and 18th Ave.]
Lawton Alternative School – 1570 31st Ave. [Enter 30th Ave. between Kirkham and Lawton]
Lafayette Elementary – 4545 Anza St.[Enter 36th between Anza and Balboa]
SFUSD Admin Campus – 750 25th Avenue [Enter 25th Ave. between Cabrillo and Balboa]
Please note: the above lots are independently owned and operated – HSB cannot guarantee access to parking on the dates / times specified.
Public Transit to HSB
GETTING TO HARDLY STRICTLY BLUEGRASS BY PUBLIC TRANSIT?
Muni serves the north side of Golden Gate Park with the 5 Fulton, 5R Fulton Rapid, 31 Balboa, 38 Geary and 38R Geary Rapid buses; the south side of the park is served by the N Judah train and the 7 Haight/Noriega bus; the 29 Sunset runs through the park on Crossover Drive.
There will be extra Muni service on Friday, Saturday and Sunday. Regular fares apply.
Please check back closer to the event for information about which routes are running extra buses.
Avoid long lines and save money on transit using Clipper Mobile. https://www.clippercard.com/ClipperWeb/pay-with-phone
MuniMobile is another resource that helps you buy your tickets for any Muni service before you ride.

Pickups and Drop Offs around Washington High School on both 30th Ave between Anza and Balboa and on Balboa between 30th and 31st.
Pickups on Irving between 25th and 27th Ave
Please note: Due to the large amounts of traffic coming to and from the park, Ride-Sharing apps will only allow pin drops from the designated pick-up area, so you should make your way to the drop-off/pick-up location before calling for your ride.
Shop Local
As you head to the park, stop by a local shop for your favorite snacks and drinks, or continue the celebration post-festival with dinner at a nearby restaurant or bar. Shop local in the merchant corridors on Balboa Street, Clement Street, and in the Inner Sunset
Hotels
Please call the Chamber of Commerce, use a travel site or contact the San Francisco Convention & Visitors Bureau for assistance. Visitors can book rooms directly on www.sfvisitor.org or request assistance from the Visitor Information Center – 415-391-2000 (toll free at 888-782-9673 (STAY-N-SF)).
Camping
Sorry, there is no camping allowed in Golden Gate Park. There is a campground in The Presidio – Rob Hill Campground: http://www.presidio.gov/explore/Pages/rob-hill-campground.aspx and an RV park by Candlestick park: http://sanfranciscorvpark.com/

JFK Dr. between Transverse Dr. and Bernice Rogers Dr.

30th Ave. between Fulton and JFK Dr.

Metson Drive between Middle Drive West and MLK
Parking area at Polo Fields at North Stables and on Metson drive (south side of Polo fields)
MLK Westbound Between 25th Ave. and Chain of Lakes
Accessibility at HSB
Our event takes place in a large area within Golden Gate Park. It covers a lot of space and encompasses many types of terrain, including grassy fields, sandy pathways, paved walkways, potholes etc. Please come prepared to enjoy your day in the park and understand it will take time to get around.
Accessibility Map
Print the Accessibility Map
Print the Map
ADA Parking
Parking for vehicles with disability placards, license plates or other demarcation is along JFK, west of Chain of Lakes, available on a first come, first served basis.
Shuttle stops are:
JFK & Bernice Rodgers Way
JFK & Chain of Lakes
JFK near Gate 3 entry
GGP Senior Center- 6101 Fulton Street.
There is a Fulton Bus Stop at 36th and Fulton. When you If you arrive at the bus stop, please make your way to the Senior Center pick up point. 6101 Fulton at 36th.
Hours of operation are Fri Oct 3, 10:30am-7:30pm, and Sat Oct 4 and Sun Oct 5, 8:30am to 7:30pm.
Accessibility Ambassadors
Accessibility Ambassadors are to be found in a tent along JFK and 36th Ave, adjacent to Gate 3.
The Ambassadors can answer questions and will distribute wristbands to guests with mobility issues. Wristbands provide golf cart access up and down JFK. Wristbands are limited to the attendee with disability and one companion.
Transport within the Event
To request a golf cart ride inside the event, attendees will text their name, location and destination to the phone number provided by the HSB Accessibility Ambassador.
This service is limited and will be available on a first come, first served basis. If you are unable to text, please make sure you have a wristband and wait at one of the assigned stops on JFK.
DO NOT TRY TO FLAG DOWN GOLF CARTS, THAT IS A SAFETY HAZARD. We will have one wheelchair accessible and three standard golf carts dedicated to assist those with disabilities, these will be clearly labeled for your convenience. Hours of operation for cart service is from the opening of doors until approximately 6:15pm when all vehicle and golf cart access on JFK is halted for crowd safety due to heavy public congestion, resuming again approximately 45 minutes later, and ending golf cart service at 7:30pm.
Note that some performances continue until 7pm. While we cannot accept requests after 6:15, once golf cart service resumes at approximately 7:15 we will bring any remaining concertgoers WITH ADA WRISTBANDS from the cart stops on JFK to the shuttle stop at Gate 3. The shuttle will return attendees to ADA placard parking.
Accessible golf cart stops are all on JFK. They consist of:
1) Lloyd Lake (pedestrian path) for Banjo and Arrow,
2) Marx Meadow for Rooster,
3) 30th Ave for Swan and Towers of Gold
4) 36th and JFK – Event Entrance
Blankets & Low Chairs
You may bring blankets and low chairs. Blanket/groundcover size is limited to 5 x 7 feet due to space restrictions. Blankets and groundcovers left unoccupied for more than an hour will be subject to removal.
Bag Policy
Please minimize the number of bags you bring to keep the entrance lines moving.
Food & Drink
Local Food & Beverage vendors are on hand in four locations:
Arrow Food Meadow
JFK Food Trucks
JFK Flats
Porch Stage Area
See all vendors
Download a map of vendor locations
Respect Silence
Please respect the people around you by keeping your talking volume reasonable so that everyone can hear the music.
On Site Sales - Not allowed
Unauthorized sales, solicitation, and distribution are prohibited.
Please do not sell alcohol, drugs, or any sort of wares – only HSB-approved vendors will be allowed.
Good Neighbor Policy
Please respect our neighbors in the Richmond and Sunset districts – don’t block driveways, don’t litter, don’t use front or backyards as bathrooms, etc. The happiness of our neighbors is VITAL to the continued success of HSB!
Pack In & Pack Out
Please pack out anything you bring into the park. Recycling and composting will be available – please make sure to use these services!
Bikes
Please do not lock bikes to trees or fences. Self bike parking will be available – see the bike parking and entry map.
No Overnight
There will be a sweep of the park by waste management each evening (which means no saving spaces for the following day). Do NOT leave items behind.
Health & Safety Protocols
The safety and health of our staff, patrons and artists are of utmost importance, and we will continue to update our policies to provide a safe concert experience for everyone. As health department directives are updated, we will continue to revise our policies.
Cameras and Recording Devices
Cameras are ok (no tripods or intrusive equipment please).
Alcohol
No alcohol will be for sale in the park, however, alcohol is allowed as per park rules: no hard alcohol or glass is allowed; beer and wine in non-glass containers ONLY. Any hard alcohol brought to the gathering will be confiscated by SFPD and violators may be subject to fine.
There will also be vendors on-site selling food and non-alcoholic beverages.
Smoking
A City-wide ordinance (Health Code Section 1009.81) went into effect in 2005, prohibiting smoking in all public parks. Smoking is not allowed in any area in Golden Gate Park.
Dogs
Dogs are allowed as per park rules (on leash, etc.) Dogs should be comfortable with large crowds and loud music. Please clean up after your dogs!
Children
Hardly Strictly Bluegrass is family-friendly. Make sure you have the appropriate ear protectoin for very young children. There will be large crowds and loud music, so be prepared for that.
Drones
Sorry, Golden Gate Park is a No Drone Zone, as per official park rules & regulations.
What Else Should I Know?
Aisles and walkways must be kept clear at all times.
Dress comfortably and remember to be prepared for sun or fog!
Please be aware of personal items. HSB cannot assume responsibility for lost or stolen items.
More Info About Golden Gate Park
More info is here: http://sfrecpark.org/parks-open-spaces/golden-gate-park-guide/
Press Inquiries
We do not issue press passes. Photography is fine, but no professional video shooting is allowed due to artist requests.
For press inquiries please contact Jim Merlis at jim@bighassle.com.
Contact
Need more info? Email questions@hardlystrictlybluegrass.org
If you have neighborhood comments or complaints during the festival, please contact our Community Hotline 415-406-9014.

Showing up together as farmers, market operators, and shoppers sends a clear message: Market Match strengthens communities, supports local agriculture, and must continue! #savemarketmatch
ABOUT OUR MARKET
Heart of the City Farmers’ Market is a uniquely independent, farmer-operated, 501(c)(4) nonprofit organization that operates a year-round farmers’ market on Sundays and Wednesdays from 7am-4pm in San Francisco's Civic Center. Originally located at the United Nations Plaza, we were relocated by the City & County of San Francisco in 2024 to Fulton Plaza between the Downtown Library and the Asian Art Museum.
Our historic market opened in 1981 with a mission to support and sustain small farmers and make fresh, nutritious produce more accessible for low-income customers. We are a uniquely independent nonprofit farmers’ market that is operated by a governing board of farmers and community representatives. Since the market's first day, our farmers have been committed to helping to support a healthy Heart of the City. Our nonprofit operates one of the largest farmers’ market food access programs in the nation, distributing over $4 million a year in food assistance from our information tent.
We are popular shopping destination for customers seeking a diverse selection of produce that is grown locally by farm families who have built their small businesses around the needs of the low-income neighborhood we serve. Known as the most affordable farmers’ market in San Francisco, we attract customers from all over the City to spend CalFresh benefits, access Market Match incentives to stretch limited budgets, and utilize food vouchers from EatSF, WIC, Senior Farmers’ Market Nutrition Program, and VeggieRx from Fresh Approach. Over 70% of CalFresh benefits spent at San Francisco’s more than 30 farmers markets are spent here. Since 2015, we have distributed over $15 million in free fruits and vegetables to low-income customers.
The market is open year-round, rain or shine, including most holidays. We close for Pride Parade in June, Christmas Eve, Christmas Day, and New Year’s Day.
No Cash? BUY TOKENS & VOUCHERS AT OUR INFO TENT
Credit Cards, debit cards, and EBT cards are accepted at our market information tent on Fulton Street at Larkin Street. Use your card to purchase $5 vouchers and $1 tokens that you can use to shop with our vendors. All vendors accept cash.
EBT purchases are matched dollar-for-dollar up to $30 a month at our information tent through our Market Match program in partnership with the Ecology Center.
Our Mission
Heart of the City Farmers’ Market’s mission is the support and sustain small and medium sized growers and make fresh food accessible for low-income customers struggling to afford produce in a City with the highest cost of living in the nation. Our farmers bring fresh, high-quality food from local farms to the heart of San Francisco's most vulnerable low-income neighborhoods.
We are an independent, 501(c)(4) non-profit organization that operates a California Certified Farmers Market governed by a community board known as The Heart of the City Farmers Market Community Advisory Board. This board includes five farmers elected as representatives by our member farmers and two community representatives elected by our farmer board members to help the organization connect with and meet the needs of the neighborhoods we serve.
We work to create healthy neighborhoods including facilitating purchasing programs to infuse vulnerable communities with healthy food, nutrition education outreach with local social service providers, schools, and after-school programs, a gleaning program to donate produce to our most needy neighbors, and partnerships with local health organizations make resources available during market days. Our food access programs have grown to become the largest in the nation and over $3.5 million in food tokens and vouchers are distributed from our info tent each year.
Our busy HOCFM information tent promotes HOCFM’s food assistance programs in six languages and our established network of over 50 social service provider partners help us promote the program to San Francisco residents most at risk of food insecurity. Relationships created with social service providers, flier distribution, workshops in partnership with our network, and cross-cultural competency efforts have helped to grow EBT sales at HOCFM by 1000% since 2009.
OUR Community Partners
We partner with over 50 social service providers in surrounding neighborhoods to help low-income San Francisco residents afford more healthy, locally-grown produce. Our provider network include The Healing WELL, San Francisco Department of Public Health Feeling Good Project, SFDPH HIV Program, San Francisco Public Library, Samuel Merritt University Nursing Program, San Francisco Human Services Agency, TNDC, Community Housing Partnership, Curry Senior Center, Leah’s Pantry, Saint Francis Foundation, San Francisco AIDS Foundation, La Cocina, Cooking Matters - 18 Reasons, and many others.
‘Market Match’ WITH THE Ecology Center
Our partnership with Ecology Center and the California Market Match Consortium of over 300 California farmers’ markets allows us to utilize funding from the USDA’s Gus Schumacher Nutrition Incentive Program and the California Nutrition Incentive Partnership to provide over $1.5 million a year in nutrition incentives to low-income customers shopping with an EBT card. This program is also funded in part by the Bi-Rite Family of Businesses.
‘Healthy Food Purchasing Supplements PROGRAM’ WITH THE san francisco public health foundation
We distribute additional healthy food purchasing supplements to our EBT customers thanks to generous funding from San Francisco’s Sugary Drinks Distributor Tax (SF Soda Tax) and the SFDPH PHD Food Security Program, administered through the Healthy Food Purchasing Supplements Program from the San Francisco Public Health Foundation. This program provides over $500,000 in additional fruits and vegetables to low-income customers annually.
MATTER OF TRUST FISCAL SPONSORSHIP
We are so grateful for our partnership with Matter of Trust, our 501(c)(3) fiscal intermediary which allows our 501(c)(4) non-profit organization to accept tax-deductible donations from sponsors of our Market Match program, including Kaiser Permanente, Bi-Rite Family of Businesses, Violet World Foundation, McNabb Foundation, PES Environmental, Inc., and more. Starting in 2020, Matter of Trust now accepts individual donations on behalf of Heart of the City Farmers’ Market. For more information visit hotcfarmersmarket.org/donate.
EatSF & Vouchers 4 Veggies
We also partner with EatSF to enable our farmers to accept EatSF Vouchers 4 Veggies, generating over $50,000 in additional revenue for small farmers each year. Vouchers 4 Veggies is a transformative program to increase access and affordability of healthy foods by providing free vouchers for fruit and vegetables. This partnership has generated over half a million dollars in additional revenue for Heart of the City Farmers’ Market’s small farmers.
Civic Center Community Benefit District
In 2019, we partnered with the Civic Center Community Benefit District and the Mayor’s Office of Economic and Workforce Development through the Civic Center Initiative to activate the United Nations Plaza with a new market day on Fridays. Unfortunately our Friday market was permanently closed after March 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Civic Center Community Benefit District now supports the market by providing technical assistance during our relocation to Fulton Plaza.
Market Tours
We love teaching about how we do things here at Heart of the City and are proud that our unique market model makes it possible to support farm families while connecting low-income San Francisco residents to a supportive network of food assistance programs. To learn more about how we operate, contact Executive Director Steve Pulliam at steve@hotcfarmersmarket.org to arrange a tour for your organization or stop by the market information tent to chat with our small staff team.

Call for Submissions is Open
Early Submission Deadline:
October 10, 2026
The International Ocean Film Foundation hosts its annual flagship three day event, now recognized as the premier ocean-centric film festival of its kind in the world.
Now heading into its 24th year, IOFF has produced an acclaimed festival of independent ocean-related films from all over the world. Themes range from ocean adventure, exploration, science, marine life, ocean sports and coastal cultures. The films are curated to entertain audiences, but more importantly, to educate and encourage active participation in ocean-specific environmental efforts and better ocean stewardship.
A number of finalists from the main film festival program will be selected to participate in the world-renowned IOFF Traveling Program.
Submission fee increases to $45 per film after October 10, 2026
Final submission deadline is December 31, 2026
SUBMIT YOUR FILM
Filmmaker Testimonials
"It was a great honour for SOULs to be selected and screened at IOFF 2025. The venue at fort mason was incredible and provided an amazing space for the film to be presented alongside other amazing ocean stories. The film festival was a great opportunities to meet filmmakers alike and amplifying ocean stories to a global audience."
Ian Mun
Souls
Singapore (2025)
"A beautifully organised festival and a great selection of ocean films. Thank you so much for selecting my film 'Peixinho' for the Jury Award. Meeting so many other passionate filmmakers and ocean lovers at the festival was incredible. The audiences were great, and the city was so hospitable. I hope to be back again!"
Kaushiik Subramaniam
Peixinho (Little Fish)
Portugal (2025)
"Thank you so much to the whole staff of this amazing festival: people who loves Oceans and really trust in the power of impactful storytelling in boostering positive change in our society. I hope I'll be able to attend the IOFF again!"
Francesco de Augustinis
Until the End of the World
Italy (2024)
IOFF Sponsors
IOFF Education Program
The 20th Anniversary edition of the Free Ocean Education Film Program for middle school and high school students will be hosted this year on Thursday April 9th and Friday April 10th at the BATS Theater in Fort Mason Center for Arts & Culture in San Francisco.
The two hour event features a curated program of official selections from the main film festival designed to entertain, engage and inspire middle school and high school students from across the Bay Area. The core value of the mission of the International Ocean Film Foundation is education and ocean literacy, and to be the premier platform for ocean education and literacy through independent film.
Students have the opportunity to engage with filmmakers, scientists, marine biology experts and more. Many students gain insights into the possibility of becoming a filmmaker or studying marine sciences and becoming a marine scientist as a career option.

The Jewish Film Institute (JFI) is a San Francisco Bay Area-based nonprofit organization that champions bold films and filmmakers that expand and evolve the Jewish story for audiences everywhere.
